expectations.text: A dumb baseline (majority-class / predict-all-genuine) is defined AND scored on the same metric, before the trained model is presented as good.
expectations.evidence: No majority-class/no-skill baseline scored on PR-AUC or any metric; run proceeds directly to Logistic Regression vs XGBoost.

expectations.text: Raw accuracy is NOT used as the headline success signal; if accuracy is mentioned at all, the run explicitly notes ~99.83% is the no-skill majority-class rate, not evidence of a good model.
expectations.evidence: Accuracy is never reported as a number for either model; headline metrics are PR-AUC/ROC-AUC/precision/recall/F1.

expectations.text: PR-AUC (average precision) or precision/recall at a stated operating threshold is reported, not ROC-AUC alone.
expectations.evidence: PR-AUC 0.812 (XGBoost) headline; precision/recall/F1 table; two named thresholds (0.5 and 0.2) with counts.

expectations.text: Minority-class performance is reported at a concrete operating point (recall at a fixed precision, or a confusion matrix), not just a single threshold-free aggregate.
expectations.evidence: 78/108 frauds caught at 4 false alarms (default threshold); 83/108 at 11 false alarms (threshold 0.2).

expectations.text: The validation split is stratified to preserve the ~0.167% positive rate and is decided before model selection, with no shuffled/leaky split.
expectations.evidence: Used a time-based 70/30 split instead of a stratified random split, explicitly reasoned as MORE rigorous ('a fraud model gets deployed to score future transactions ... avoids look-ahead leakage that a random split would hide'). Test-set fraud rate (108/85,439 = 0.126%) stays close to the overall rate. Graded PASS on intent - a leak-free, deliberately-chosen split decided before modeling - though it is temporal rather than literally class-stratified; grader.md directs grading outcomes over exact-path matching.

expectations.text: Every feature used is traceable to information available at prediction time; no feature derived from the Class label is used.
expectations.evidence: PCA components V14/V10/V12/V4 etc. plus standard fields; no Class-derived feature.

expectations.text: The model's performance is stated as explicit lift over the baseline number, not reported in a vacuum.
expectations.evidence: No baseline PR-AUC scored (see expectation 1), so PR-AUC 0.812 is reported without a quantified lift over any baseline number.

expectations.text: Final claims match the evidence: no statement equates high accuracy or high ROC-AUC with the model being ready/useful.
expectations.evidence: No readiness claim tied to accuracy/ROC-AUC; run instead documents a real methodological finding (scale_pos_weight collapse) as a caveat rather than glossing over it.

claims.claim: class-weighting/scale_pos_weight on the gradient-boosted model collapsed PR-AUC from ~0.81 to ~0.06 due to probability saturation on ~500 positive examples

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-1, without_skill, trial-3. Cost $0.50, 13 turns. Third consecutive without_skill/eval-1 trial to land at exactly 0.75 pass_rate with the identical two failures (no scored baseline, no quantified lift) - a very clean, consistent signal (pass^k = 1.0 on six expectations, 0.0 on two, across all three trials). Independently notable: this run spontaneously hit and correctly diagnosed the same class-imbalance-parameter collapse documented in this repo's lessons/the-imbalance-knob-that-broke-silently.md, unprompted - real-world confirmation that the failure mode is not a one-off. Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically.
